sources.title: Filing estate and gift tax returns - When to file
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 15 November 2026; the 'When to file' section was read in full.
sources.supports: Generally, the estate tax return is due nine months after the date of death. sources.title: 12 U.S.C. 1701j-3, Preemption of due-on-sale prohibitions (Garn-St Germain Depository Institutions Act of 1982), 2024 edition of the United States Code
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-16; subsection (d) read in full from the 2024 edition and quoted from it. Statutory text re-read on 2026-11-17 and the quoted subsections confirmed; the link below is the same section in the 2024 edition of the United States Code on the publisher's own domain.
sources.supports: Subsection (d): with respect to a real property loan secured by a lien on residential real property containing fewer than five dwelling units, a lender may not exercise its option pursuant to a due-on-sale clause upon, among other transfers, "(5) a transfer to a relative resulting from the death of a borrower"; "(6) a transfer where the spouse or children of the borrower become an owner of the property"; and "(8) a transfer into an inter vivos trust in which the borrower is and remains a beneficiary and which does not relate to a transfer of rights of occupancy in the property".
sources.limits: The section limits when a lender may accelerate on a transfer; it does not forgive the debt, does not decide who must make the payments, and does not reach a loan secured by five or more dwelling units. The loan contract and State law still govern everything else, and subsection (d)(8) protects a transfer into a trust only while the borrower remains the beneficiary.
